parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes a new Border Security Command to disrupt criminal smuggling gangs, additional caseworkers to clear the asylum backlog, a fast-track returns and enforcement unit, and reforms to the points-based immigration system linking it to skills policy to reduce net migration.

citations.quote: We will create a new Border Security Command, with hundreds of new investigators, intelligence officers, and cross-border police officers.
Labour will reduce net migration. We will reform the points-based immigration system so that it is fair and properly managed, with and by linking immigration and skills policy.

results.headline: Labour pledges swift, firm and fair asylum system
results.quote: Labour will restore order to the asylum system so that it operates swiftly, firmly, and fairly; and the rules are properly enforced.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives propose a legally binding annual cap on migration that falls each year, continued removal of illegal migrants to Rwanda, clearing the asylum backlog within six months, and raising salary thresholds for skilled worker and family visas automatically with inflation.

citations.quote: We will introduce a binding, legal cap on migration, set on work and family visas so public services are protected whilst we bring the skills our businesses and the NHS needs.
The cap will fall every year of the next Parliament and cannot be breached.

results.headline: Conservatives pledge legal migration cap to guarantee falling numbers
results.quote: Introduce a legal cap on migration to guarantee that numbers will fall every year, so public services are protected while bringing in the skills we need.

results.headline: Conservative MP credits ETA scheme as Conservative border reform
results.quote: The ETA scheme was introduced by the Conservative Government to secure and modernise Britain's borders.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose scrapping the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, ending the Hostile Environment, replacing salary thresholds with a flexible merit-based work visa system, tackling the asylum backlog with a three-month service standard, and expanding safe and legal routes for refugees.

citations.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees, helping to prevent dangerous Channel crossings.

Replace the Conservatives' arbitrary salary threshold with a more flexible merit-based system for work visas, with the relevant department working with employers in each sector to address specific needs as part of a long-term workforce strategy that also focuses on education and training to address skills gaps from within the UK.

results.headline: Lib Dems pledge to scrap Rwanda scheme and uphold Refugee Convention
results.quote: Scrap the Conservatives' Illegal Migration Act and their Rwanda scheme, uphold the Refugee Convention, and provide safe and legal routes to sanctuary for refugees.

parties.name: Plaid Cymru
parties.summary: Plaid Cymru opposes the Rwanda deportation policy and the hostile environment, calls for repeal of the Nationality and Borders Act and Illegal Migration Act, supports safe routes for asylum seekers, and advocates for Wales to have devolved powers over migration including its own shortage occupation list and visa schemes.

citations.quote: We would support the repeal of previous punitive legislation which is part of the hostile environment, including the Nationality and Borders Act 2022 and the Illegal Migration Act 2023.
Wales should have greater powers over migration - including the ability to determine our own Shortage Occupation List and granting the Welsh Government the ability to manage its own visa schemes.

results.headline: Plaid Cymru opposes Rwanda deportations and demands UK uphold Refugee Treaty
results.quote: Plaid Cymru strongly oppose the Conservative UK Government's proposals and attitudes towards asylum seekers and refugees, including deportation to Rwanda and the general hostile environment created. We believe that the UK should uphold the commitments made when it signed up to the Refugee Treaty in 1951.
